newsitem.title: USA: Tampa, Fla., stadium bond sale delayed by lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Tampa, Fla., stadium bond sale delayed by lawsuit.

text.p: Florida's Tampa Sports Authority will postpone a $168 million revenue bond sale for a new football stadium until litigation over the finance plan is settled, authority finance director Henry Saavedra said Friday.
The sale had been expected by mid-November, with Smith Barney Inc as senior manager for the negotiated deal.
But a lawsuit challenging the use of sales tax money for the debt service is still pending in Florida's 2nd District Court of Appeals.
"While it's still out there, we're not going to issue the bonds," Saavedra said. However, he said, "We feel confident it should be done by the end of the year."

On Sept 3, Hillsborough County voters approved a half-cent sales tax increase that will raise $2.7 billion over 30 years for schools, roads, public safety and the new stadium for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Former Tampa Mayor sued unsuccessfully in August to block the referendum. He sued again last month, arguing both times that the plan would unconstitutionally use public money to benefit the private, for-profit football team.

The latest suit was dismissed earlier this month by a Hillsborough Circuit Court judge, who said it raised no new issues. Poe appealed, and Hillsborough County attorneys have asked for fast-track status that could settle the appeal by the end of October. County Attorney Emeline Acton said she if confident the county will win.
Saavedra said the authority does not want to risk having the court reject the financing plan after the bonds are issued, although he considers that unlikely.
"In the one in a million shot that he (Poe) wins, we're in serious trouble," he said.
Groundbreaking for the stadium took place Monday. On Wednesday the authority formally approved a contract with the construction firm of Huber, Hunt & Nichols to build the arena.
Saavedra said construction would proceed, funded with $20 million the authority raised in a land sale.
"We feel that will carry us to decision time. We're not going to stop," he said.
